SLM alloys possess a fine grain organization and thus a strong grain boundary strengthening effect is obtained.

After solid solution treated at higher temperature, the Ostwald ripening inevitably occurs as the solute sites in the parent phase are vacated with the massive generation of complex precipitated phases, and the Al–Si eutectic breaks up and disintegrates to form numerous microscopic Si particles.

After solution treated at higher temperature, the formation of AlFe0.27Ni0.77 means that a large number of solute atoms were desolvated and Si was able to diffuse through the matrix, thus enabling Ostwald ripening to take place. ... the strength of the alloy is therefore significantly reduced.

horizontal tensile strengths of the alloys in the as-built, annealed, solution treated and T6 states are 589 MPa, 524 MPa, 325 MPa, and 292 MPa, respectively, showing a tendency of gradual decreasing.

The maintenance of the Al–Si eutectic morphology ensured the mechanical properties of the alloy, and the alloy still possessed UTS of 524 MPa and 517 MPa in both the horizontal and vertical directions in the annealed state.
This partly explains the abrupt decrease in strength of solid solution alloys.
